previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after being found lethargic at a rehab facility, where she had been off her baseline oxygen. Initial improvement with Narcan suggested opioid-related sedation, but further evaluation revealed multiple contributing factors: a recent increase in lithium dose, right lower lobe pneumonia, and possible hypoxia from a pleural effusion. She was treated with intravenous antibiotics, supplemental oxygen, and respiratory support. Her mental status improved significantly by hospital day 2. Lithium was restarted at a reduced dose per psychiatric consultation, and methadone was gradually resumed. She remained afebrile, with improving white blood cell count, and was discharged to extended care on oral antibiotics and adjusted medications. A new knee brace was fitted prior to discharge.

Brief Hospital Course:

RUQ/chest pain and increased oxygen requirement.  At baseline

weaned down to her baseline.  Given her weight and poor quality 
of CXR images, a VQ scan was not performed.  D-dimer was 
elevated.  She has a history of allergy to IV contrast and 
intially refused to undergo premedication for dye due to concern 
about side effects from prednisone.  Due to concern for PE 
without ability to obtain adequate imaging the night of 
admission she was started on a heparin drip empirically.  She 
was ruled out for MI with two sets of negative cardiac enzymes.  


The morning after admission b/l lower extremity US were 
performed which showed no DVT.  She then agreed to undergo 
premedication for her dye allergy and underwent a CTA which 
showed no PE.  The heparin drip was stopped.  She diuresed 
gently due to concern for volume overload causing some of her 
dyspnea and tranistioned back to her home dose of lasix 40 mg 
daily.

# Allergic reaction to dye: The patient underwent a CTA with dye 
(to rule out PE as above) after premedication for dye allergy 
during this admission.  Premedication consisted of prednisone 
30mg (to be given 16hr, 8hr, 2hr pre-scan), Ranitidine 150mg PO 
(1hr pre-scan), Benadryl 50mg PO (1hr pre-scan).  After the 
study she developed an erythematous, blanching rash on her torso 
and extremities.  No SOB or wheezing.  She was monitored for 
several days after the developement of her rash.  The rash 
remained stable and she was given additional doses of benadryl 
and ranitidine.  She will follow up with her primary doctor for 
resolution of her rash.

# Right-sided Chest/RUQ pain: The patient was ruled out for PE 
as above.  A CXR and CTA showed no evidence of infection/PNA.  
She underwent an abdominal US which showed fatty infiltration, 
but no acute process.  She has a history of hepatitis B and 
hepatitis C and had mildly elevated LFTs.  It is unclear what 
cuased her pain.  It slowly resolved prior to discharge.
